question: How soon should I file a federal labour standards complaint about wages that were due but never paid?
generated_answer:
The time limit for filing a complaint under the Canada Labour Code is generally 6 months from the date the wages were due. However, if the employer has not paid the wages and has not provided a reason for non-payment, the time limit may be extended. It is recommended to file a complaint as soon as possible to ensure that the matter is addressed in a timely manner.

If you are unsure about the specific time limit or need assistance with filing a complaint, you can contact the Labour Program's Call Centre at 1-800-641-4049 or visit their website for more information.

Here is the relevant section from the Canada Labour Code:

**Canada Labour Code, Part III - Labour Standards, Division 1 - Wages, Section 134**

**134. (1)** A complaint under this Part may be made by an employee or former employee who alleges that an employer has failed to pay wages that were due and payable under this Part.

**(2)** A complaint under subsection (1) must be made within six months after the wages were due and payable, unless the employer has not paid the wages and has not provided a reason for non-payment, in which case the time limit may be extended.

**(3)** The time limit under subsection (2) may be extended by the Minister if the employee or former employee has made reasonable efforts to obtain payment from the employer and has not been able to do so.

**(4)** The Minister may, in exceptional circumstances, extend the time limit under subsection (2) if the employee or former employee has a valid reason for not filing the complaint within the time limit.

**(5)** A complaint under subsection (1) must be in writing and must include the following information:

**(a)** the name and address of the employee or former employee making the complaint;

**(b)** the name and address of the employer;

**(c)** a description of the wages that were due and payable, including the amount and the date they were due;

**(d)** a description of the efforts made by the employee or former employee to obtain payment from the employer;

**(e)** any other relevant information that supports the complaint.

**(6)** The Minister may require the employee or former employee to provide additional information or evidence to support the complaint.

**(7)** The Minister may investigate the complaint and may make a decision on the matter.

**(8)** If the Minister finds that the employer has failed to pay wages that were due and payable, the Minister may order the employer to pay the wages, plus interest, and may impose penalties if the employer has not provided a reason for non-payment.

**(9)** The Minister's decision on a complaint under this section is final and binding, subject to appeal to the Federal Court.

It is recommended to consult with a labour lawyer or contact the Labour Program's Call Centre for personalized advice and assistance with filing a complaint.
